messages.author: 9cd7abbc55138f90
messages.subject: pbdDMAT runs too slow
parts:
Hello everyone,
       
           These days I did some experiments on pbdDMAT but found that the distributed matrix multiplication is too slow which is out of tolerance and abnormal.
           Then I did a little experiment to find what is wrong and I found that the serial matrix multiplication provided by pbdDMAT is very very slowly. There must be something wrong. Could you help me find the problem? If the problem can not be solved, the package is not practical for me to use.
         
           The program is fairly simple(See matprod.r in attachment). I paste it as below:

### SHELL> mpiexec -np 2 Rscript --vanilla [...].r

# Initialize process grid
library(pbdDMAT, quiet=F)

args <- commandArgs()

#print(args)
comm.print(args[6])
comm.print(args[7])

# Global matrix dimension
size <- as.numeric(args[6])
blockfactor <- as.numeric(args[7])

init.grid()

# Generate a random matrix common to all processes and distribute it.
# This approach should only be used while learning the pbdDMAT package.
comm.set.seed(123,diff=TRUE)
# We generate a global big square matrix.
dx <- ddmatrix("rnorm", mean=0,sd=10,ncol=size,nrow=size,bldim=blockfactor)
print(dx)
barrier()
t1 <- proc.time()[3]
#dx %*% dx
barrier()
t2 <- proc.time()[3]

%Measure the time it costs
comm.print(t2 - t1, all.rank=T)

x <- matrix(c(0),ncol=size,nrow=size)
t3 <- proc.time()[3]
x %*% x
t4 <- proc.time()[3]

%Measure the serial time cost
comm.print(t4 - t3, all.rank=T)

# Finish
finalize()


        and I run it with the following command:

time ./runtest.sh singlehost 1 matprod.r "10000 10000"

       which equals the following command:

/usr/lib64/openmpi/bin/mpirun -mca btl_tcp_if_include eth0,lo -mca btl_tcp_disable_family 6 -hostfile singlehost -np 1 /home/hadoop/bin/R-3.1.1/lib64/R/bin/Rscript ./matprod.r 10000 10000

Then in the program, it will do a two square matrices multiplication whoes sizes are both 10,000 * 10,000. In the distributed version, the block size is also 10,000 * 10,000 which means the distribued multiplication will fallback to a serial version.

The performance of distributed matrix multiplication is 23 minutes on our machines, which is too slow. The same multiplication runned by a CBLAS program costs just about 4 minutes. R-pbd is far too slow. There must be something wrong! Could you give a clue on the problem? Thank you very much!
 
Best wishes,
                             Dale Wang

messages.author: 04ee6652802764c3
messages.subject: Re: pbdDMAT runs too slow
parts:
Hi Dale,

Without knowing some more information, it's hard to say exactly what's going on.  However, I do wonder if you're using the same BLAS library.  If you don't sort of go out of your way to use a different one, R will use the reference implementation of the BLAS.  And pbdR will just use whichever BLAS R is using.  Did you notice a large difference between R and pbdR timings?

My usual production machines are down for maintenance, but running this on my Sandy Bridge laptop using the Atlas implementation and OMP_NUM_THREADS=1, I get:

C: 160.642170
R: 159.709
pbdR: 159.142

The files that I used for this benchmark are attached.  Build the C program via cc cprod.c -lblas, and simply execute it.  Run the R script via Rscript prod.r 10000.  The pbdR one was executed as mpirun -np 1 Rscript pbdprod.r 10000 10000.  Some (but not a staggering amount) of MPI overhead with the pbdR solution is to be expected, so the fact that pbdR was faster than R here is again probably just "getting lucky" and up to the variability of the machine.  Likewise for C and R (which I would expect to be epsilon faster on average).

--Drew

messages.author: 9cd7abbc55138f90
messages.subject: Re: pbdDMAT runs too slow
parts:
Hi Drew,
   
Thank you for your reply. I followed your guide and checked the BLAS library used by R. It is libRblas.so. And I find that library is very slow... It is what makes the matrix multiplication very slowly. The 10,000 * 10,000 matrix multiplication takes about 23 minutes. So it is not Rpbd's fault.

I searched on the Internet and link the libRblas.so to /usr/lib64/libblas.so to make it use native blas library. The multiplication time becomes normal. The speed of R and rpbd are the same as C code provided by you.

Could you give me some advice on configuring R to make it more efficient?
Thank you very much.

Best wishes,
                                      Dale

messages.author: 04ee6652802764c3
messages.subject: Re: pbdDMAT runs too slow
parts:
The R Installation manual offers some useful advice:  http://cran.r-project.org/doc/manuals/R-admin.html

The biggest performance improvement will probably come from using a high performance BLAS and LAPACK implementation, such as MKL.  Compiling R with a better compiler (e.g., icc and ifort on Intel hardware) would gain some small (but free) performance gains.  Compiling with --disable-R-shlib will probably help.  Compiling with --disable-R-profiling and --disable-memory-profiling may help, but probably not enough to warrant their absence.

-Drew
